intro: This week’s intelligence digest highlights significant shifts in retail and AI sectors, including California’s legal challenge against Amazon for price fixing and major investments by Amazon and Google in AI startup Anthropic. Additionally, the luxury market sees evolving dynamics with falling lab-grown diamond prices and renewed consumer interest driven by World Diamond Day.

readOneThing.title: California Accuses Amazon of Price Fixing in Legal Filing

items.title: California Accuses Amazon of Price Fixing in Legal Filing
bullets: California filed a legal complaint against Amazon on April 20, 2026, accusing the company of pressuring brands to fix product prices.
The complaint specifically names brands like Levi’s and Hanes as being pressured to encourage competing retailers to raise prices on certain products.
This legal action reflects ongoing scrutiny of Amazon's market practices and adds to previous investigations into e-commerce price manipulation.

items.title: Wholesale lab-grown diamond prices down 14%
bullets: The Q1 2026 Lab-Grown Diamond Wholesale Price List reveals a 14% decline in lab-grown diamond prices, signaling a moderation in market volatility.
The 3-carat round diamonds experienced the steepest price drop, falling 28% year-over-year, an improvement from the over 40% decline in Q1 2025.
After nearly a decade of continuous price declines, the lab-grown diamond market is stabilizing with measured demand growth and producers focusing on higher quality output.

items.title: Amazon Plans to Invest Up to $25 Billion in Anthropic
bullets: Amazon has announced plans to invest up to $25 billion in the AI startup Anthropic to advance artificial intelligence technologies.
Anthropic has committed to spending $100 billion on Amazon technologies to support the development and deployment of AI systems.
This investment represents one of the largest financial commitments in the AI sector, reflecting rapid growth and competition in the industry.

items.title: How COS Orchestrates a Global Elevated Store Experience
bullets: The brand emphasizes a localized approach to portfolio management to tailor the store experience to different markets worldwide.
Based in London, COS is executing this strategy across multiple regions to elevate its retail footprint over the coming years.
Read the full article for details.

items.title: Marketplace Briefing: Amazon’s seller count falls as revenue concentrates among top sellers
bullets: Amazon's active seller count on its marketplace declined from 584,000 in January 2025 to 500,000 by March 2026 amid rising fees and operational costs.
Marketplace Pulse reported that fewer than 8,000 sellers now generate roughly half of Amazon's U.S. third-party gross merchandise volume, down from about 15,000 sellers a few years ago.
In 2025, third-party seller services, including commissions and advertising fees, generated $172 billion for Amazon, accounting for approximately 24% of the company's total net sales.

items.title: Google pours up to $40 billion into ChatGPT rival Anthropic
bullets: Google is investing up to $40 billion into Anthropic, the AI company that developed the ChatGPT rival Claude.
This investment, combined with Amazon's $25 billion pledge, will provide Anthropic with up to $65 billion in funding within weeks.
The large-scale funding from major tech companies highlights the growing competition in the AI chatbot market.

items.title: World Diamond Day prompts surge in jewellery interest
bullets: The Natural Diamond Council announced the successful launch of the inaugural World Diamond Day, which aimed to promote diamond jewellery globally.
The event led to a notable surge in consumer interest and sales of diamond jewellery, as reported by industry sources on April 20, 2026.
Read the full article for details.

items.title: Pine Labs acquires ecommerce enabler Shopflo for Rs 88 crore
bullets: Shopflo, founded in 2021, serves 1,000 direct-to-consumer brands and offers payment checkout, discounts, loyalty programs, and payment orchestration features.
Following the acquisition, Pine Labs Online will have about 400 employees, and Shopflo's founders will step down from executive roles but remain as advisors.
